decisions.reason: As a cardboard quarter-pallet display close to the firm's core business, it is likely to be retained because prior development and public presentation create commitment and any weaker sales can be seen as temporary.
Although more specialized because of the pegboard back, it still fits the established display portfolio, so sunk development effort and visible market introduction favor continuing it.
This is a standard cardboard shelf display in the firm's main product area, making it easy for management to justify staying the course after already investing and showcasing it.
The eighth-pallet format is somewhat narrower in application, but it remains part of the core display line and disappointing demand can plausibly be blamed on temporary retail conditions.
A wooden display pallet sits less centrally in a paper-products firm's announced direction, so despite prior investment it is the easiest product to cut in a portfolio review.

The media-focused quarter-pallet display faces a narrower end market, but management is still likely to persist because it has already committed resources and can interpret weak results as category-specific and temporary.
